title: A role change across connected systems
question: An employee changes role while a session and an entitlement remain active. Which configuration changes and verification evidence establish removal of the old access?
scenario: A finance approver moves to an audit role at 09:00. HR records the move and the identity platform removes the approver group, but an application entitlement and a session issued before the move remain active. The service’s desired-state configuration says auditors may view records but may not approve payments.
focalRelation: The identity lifecycle event is operationalized through controlled configuration changes across every downstream entitlement and session, followed by evidence that effective access now matches desired state.

nodes.label: Authoritative role change
nodes.detail: The mover event changes the employee’s approved duties and initiates removal of finance-approver access.

nodes.label: Directory group removed
nodes.detail: The identity platform removes the approver group and records the approved provisioning change.

nodes.label: Application entitlement
nodes.detail: A separately stored approval entitlement must be reconciled and removed; the directory change alone does not prove this state changed.

nodes.label: Existing session
nodes.detail: A previously issued session retains approval capability until revoked, expired, or re-evaluated by the application.

nodes.label: Effective-access verification
nodes.detail: Compare directory, application entitlement, active session, and a negative approval test against the auditor desired state.

lanes.label: Lifecycle authority
lanes.rule: The role event changes approved access but is not proof of downstream completion.

lanes.label: Controlled configuration
lanes.rule: Each configuration item must reach the approved desired state.

lanes.label: Effective runtime access
lanes.rule: Existing sessions and cached permissions require explicit treatment.

lanes.label: Verification
lanes.rule: Closure requires observed effective access, not only a successful workflow status.

states.title: The mover event changes the target state
states.caption: At 09:00 the employee should retain auditor viewing but lose payment approval.

states.title: Directory state changes first
states.caption: Removing the group is necessary, but the application entitlement and live session remain independent configuration subjects.

states.title: Remove entitlement and revoke runtime authority
states.caption: Apply approved changes to the application record and session, retaining change evidence for each subject.

states.title: Test effective access against desired state
states.caption: A negative approval test plus state evidence establishes removal; ticket completion alone does not.

variants.label: Service account ownership change
variants.changedFact: A service owner leaves, the directory owner field changes, but the old owner still holds a vaulted credential and active administrative token.

states.title: Metadata changed; authority persists
states.caption: The ownership record does not revoke credential copies or active tokens.

states.title: Rotate, revoke, and test
states.caption: Rotate the credential, revoke active tokens, reconcile entitlements, and verify the former owner cannot administer the service.

nodes.label: Service owner departed
nodes.detail: The departure changes accountable ownership and requires removal of the old owner’s runtime authority.

nodes.label: Ownership metadata updated
nodes.detail: The service record names a new owner, but metadata alone does not revoke the former owner’s credential.

nodes.label: Service administrative entitlement
nodes.detail: Reconcile who may administer the service under the new owner assignment.

nodes.label: Former owner token
nodes.detail: The old runtime token remains capable until rotated or revoked.

nodes.label: Negative service-admin test
nodes.detail: Verify the former owner credential fails while authorized service operation remains available.

edges.label: metadata is evidence but not effective revocation

states.title: One credential subject remains outside reconciliation
states.caption: Directory, entitlement, and browser-session changes do not revoke the independent API token.

states.title: Revoke the token and test effective denial
states.caption: Bring every credential subject to desired state and verify that payment approval fails while allowed audit access remains.

nodes.label: Mover target state
nodes.detail: The employee may audit records but may no longer approve payments through any credential.

nodes.label: Scheduled API token
nodes.detail: A noninteractive token issued under the old approver role still authorizes payment approval.

nodes.label: Effective payment-approval test
nodes.detail: Revoke every old-role credential and prove the approval action is denied.

prediction.prompt: Can the role change be closed after the directory group is removed?

options.label: Yes; the authoritative directory is the only state that matters
options.feedback: The directory is authoritative for intent, but the application and session can retain effective authority independently.

options.label: No; reconcile the app entitlement and session, then verify effective access
options.feedback: Correct. The lifecycle event must become controlled changes across each downstream subject and a verified runtime outcome.

options.label: Yes after the session eventually expires, without checking
options.feedback: Unmeasured expiry leaves a period of unauthorized authority and no evidence that the entitlement itself was removed.

prediction.hint: List every place that can still authorize the old action.

transfer.prompt: For the departed service owner, which action proves the old administrative authority is removed?

options.label: Update the service owner field and retain the existing runtime credential
options.feedback: Ownership metadata does not invalidate copied secrets, tokens, or privileges.

options.label: Close the departure after automation reports success without access testing
options.feedback: Workflow success is administrative evidence; it must be reconciled with effective configuration and runtime access.

options.label: Rotate the credential, revoke tokens, reconcile entitlement, and run a negative access test
options.feedback: Correct. Each authority-bearing subject reaches desired state and the outcome is tested.

transfer.hint: Distinguish the desired owner record from every credential and session that still carries authority.

retry.prompt: A third review confirms the user entitlement and browser session are gone, but a scheduled API token issued under the old role still approves payments. Is the mover complete?

options.label: No; revoke the token, reconcile every credential subject, and verify payment denial
options.feedback: Correct. Effective authority remains until the old-role token is removed and the protected action is tested.

options.label: Yes; removing the interactive entitlement and session completes the mover event
options.feedback: The surviving API token is another configuration and credential subject carrying the old authority.

options.label: Yes; leave the token active until its normal expiry because directory state is correct
options.feedback: Waiting preserves prohibited effective access and does not meet the changed desired state.

retry.hint: Inventory every runtime credential and entitlement that can exercise the old role, not only interactive sessions.

takeaway: Identity lifecycle events define desired access. Configuration management operationalizes the change across directory, application, credentials, and sessions; verification establishes the effective result.
assumptions: The HR mover event is authoritative and approved.
The application entitlement and session can survive a directory group change.
The negative test is authorized and does not perform a prohibited business transaction.

treatmentDispositions.rationale: The state model makes the assigned lifecycle-to-configuration relationship concrete across distinct subjects and requires verification of effective removal.
